title: Constructibility and base-change equality of the geometrically reduced fibre locus
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a finitely presented homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. For a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ let $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ be its residue field [def-weil-residue-field], and put
$$E_{\mathrm{red}}(B/A)=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A\mid B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)\text{ is geometrically reduced over }\kappa(\mathfrak p)\}.$$
Here geometrically reduced means that the spectrum is reduced after every field extension, as in [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and $\operatorname{Spec}$ is [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $E_{\mathrm{red}}(B/A)$ is constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Moreover, for every homomorphism $a:A\to A'$ of commutative rings, with $B'=B\otimes_A A'$, one has
$$E_{\mathrm{red}}(B'/A')=(\operatorname{Spec}a)^{-1}(E_{\mathrm{red}}(B/A)).$$
No flatness, injectivity or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0579 (lemma-geometrically-reduced-constructible) and 0576 (lemma-base-change-fibres-geometrically-reduced), affine ring form. In 0579 the locus is locally constructible; on the affine (hence qcqs) base it is constructible by Properties Tag 054C (lemma-locally-constructible).

proof.text: Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $f:X\to T$ and $E_f=\{\mathfrak p\mid X_{\bar{\mathfrak p}}\text{ is reduced}\}$. By [lem-trf-affine-geometric-fibre-reduced-comparison], $f$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation, its base is qcqs, and $E_f=E_{\mathrm{red}}(B/A)$. The comparison and the projection identifications hold for arbitrary ring maps.

source.place: Tags 0579 and 0576: affine fibre interpretation and finiteness hypotheses

proof.text: Choose $n,m$, relations $F_j$ and an $A$-algebra isomorphism $\alpha:A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(F_1,\ldots,F_m)\cong B$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Apply [lem-trf-presentation-noetherian-coefficient-model] to this specified presentation, obtaining its Noetherian coefficient subring $A_0$, finitely presented $A_0$-algebra $B_0$ and $A$-algebra isomorphism $B_0\otimes_{A_0}A\cong B$. Let $f_0:X_0=\operatorname{Spec}B_0\to T_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ and $g:\operatorname{Spec}A\to T_0$. The affine comparison makes $f_0$ quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation, and identifies $f$ with its base change along $g$, including the projection to $\operatorname{Spec}A$.

Put $E_0=\{t\in T_0\mid (X_0)_{\bar t}\text{ is reduced}\}$. Since $f_0$ has the two morphism finiteness properties from Step 2, [lem-trf-reduced-fibre-locus-closed-stratum-alternative] applies: every irreducible closed subset of $T_0$ has a nonempty relatively open part contained in $E_0$ or disjoint from it. The coefficient-model node gives that $A_0$ is Noetherian, so the one-member affine cover of $T_0$ meets the hypotheses of [lem-trf-noetherian-constructible-subset-criterion]. That criterion makes $E_0$ constructible.

source.place: Tag 0579, Noetherian closed-subset criterion and Tags 0577--0578

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-geometric-reduced-fibre-locus-base-change] to $f_0$ and $g$ in the model square of Step 2. The $A$-algebra isomorphism there identifies its projection and geometric fibres with those of $f$, so the equality is $E_f=g^{-1}(E_0)$. Since $E_0$ is constructible by Step 3, [lem-pur-scheme-constructible-preimage] makes its inverse image constructible. Step 1 identifies it with $E_{\mathrm{red}}(B/A)$.

source.place: Tag 0579, return from the Noetherian model using 0576; Morphisms Tag 054I

proof.text: For an arbitrary $a:A\to A'$, set $B'=B\otimes_A A'$. The affine comparison identifies $\operatorname{Spec}B'\to\operatorname{Spec}A'$ with the base-change projection of $f$: its ring map is $c\mapsto1\otimes c$, and the other projection has ring map $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. It also identifies both ring loci with their reduced geometric-fibre loci. Apply [lem-trf-geometric-reduced-fibre-locus-base-change] to obtain $E_{\mathrm{red}}(B'/A')=(\operatorname{Spec}a)^{-1}(E_{\mathrm{red}}(B/A))$. Neither comparison nor equality requires flatness or finite presentation of $a$. The comparison for $A'\to B'$ uses its arbitrary-ring-map clause, so no separate finite-presentation assertion for $B'$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0576, arbitrary base change with affine projections from Schemes Tag 01I4
